source.title: Parameter Reduction Improves Vision Transformers: A Comparative Study of Sharing and Width Reduction

record.tranche_reason: The study compares validation accuracy and training-time behavior across parameter-reduced ViT-B/16 variants and a baseline, but does not reproduce a systematic double-descent sweep.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results comparing parameter counts and training trajectories, which bear on V1 and V2. It does not locate an interpolation threshold or report a fall-rise-fall curve. Cited results about double descent are not extracted as rows. Top-5 accuracy, throughput, memory, and accuracy-per-parameter are not measures of the claimed test-error curves.
record.test_reason: The study compares one 86.6M ViT-B/16 baseline with two 58.2M MLP-reduced variants that also change architecture. It has no size sweep, interpolation threshold, sample-size variation, noise or regularization sweep, or test-error curve with a second descent. The baseline's late-training decline is ordinary overfitting within 300 epochs, with no second fall. Double descent is only cited as context the results 'align with'. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: for ViT-B/16 on ImageNet-1K under one recipe, MLP sharing or width reduction slightly improves accuracy and greatly improves training stability, suggesting the baseline is overparameterized.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares specific MLP-sharing and width-reduction architectures against one ViT-B/16 baseline; it does not perform the original systematic size, data, or epoch double-descent sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that the result is limited to ViT-B/16 on ImageNet-1K under one training recipe and leave broader model-size and architecture studies for future work.

fits_no_version.finding: Two 58.2M-parameter MLP-reduced ViT-B/16 variants slightly beat the 86.6M baseline on ImageNet-1K top-1 (81.47 and 81.25 vs 81.05).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reducing or sharing MLP capacity in ViT-B/16 on ImageNet-1K slightly improves accuracy (non-monotonic accuracy with parameter count at two points).

fits_no_version.finding: The baseline's validation accuracy peaks at epoch 219 and then degrades while loss rises. The reduced models stay stable to epoch 300.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger ViT-B/16 MLPs show late-training validation degradation (overfitting) that reduced-capacity variants avoid.

record.problems: Only one baseline size and two parameter-reduction designs are compared; the study does not locate an interpolation threshold or measure a full double-descent curve. It is limited to one model, dataset, and training recipe, and reports results over two seeds.
record.rows_left_out: No additional directly relevant results left out. Peak epochs are reported in Table 2, but peak timing alone does not measure either claimed curve.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep, no interpolation threshold, and no test-error peak or second descent; only two sizes are compared.
No full epoch-wise test-error trajectory showing a second descent. The baseline only declines after epoch 219 through epoch 300.
Training sample size is not varied.
No other model classes and no capacity sweep past interpolation.
No label-noise, regularization-tuning or multiple-peak analysis.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 is overturned. Double descent appears only in the related work and introduction as motivation. The training uses heavy augmentation, and no interpolation of the training set is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No systematic model-size sweep, interpolation threshold, or complete fall-rise-fall test-error curve.
No complete test-error trajectory showing whether error falls, rises, and falls again; the reported dynamics cover validation accuracy/loss and peak-to-final change.
Training sample size is not varied.
No general comparison across model classes or capacity sweep.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested across axes.
Label noise, multiple peaks, and optimally tuned regularization are not tested.
No alternative effective-parameter count or corresponding curve is evaluated.

rows.subject: Baseline
rows.operation_detail: Baseline in comparison with two parameter-reduced ViT-B/16 variants.
rows.note: A single baseline comparison does not establish a model-size curve or interpolation threshold.
rows.check: A single baseline accuracy is one point, not a model-size curve. Serves only as a comparator.

rows.subject: GroupedMLP
rows.operation_detail: Shares MLP weights between adjacent transformer blocks, reducing 12 unique MLPs to 6.
rows.note: The reduced model has higher reported accuracy, but this comparison does not establish the claimed curve.
rows.check: Two points (86.6M vs 58.2M) with weight sharing, which changes architecture, not just size. No interpolation threshold or fall-rise-fall shape can be read.

rows.subject: ShallowMLP
rows.operation_detail: Halves the MLP hidden dimension from 3072 to 1536.
rows.note: The reduced model has higher reported accuracy, but this comparison does not establish the claimed curve.
rows.check: Width halving gives a second model size only. Two points cannot show a double-descent curve.

rows.subject: Baseline
rows.operation_detail: Reports peak-to-final validation-accuracy change during training.
rows.note: The text says validation accuracy peaks at epoch 219 and then degrades; the reported gap alone does not establish an epoch-wise double-descent curve.
rows.check: The peak-to-final gap is a stability metric. The baseline's peak at epoch 219 then decline to 300 shows only a single rise (overfitting), not a second descent.

rows.subject: GroupedMLP
rows.operation_detail: Reports peak-to-final validation-accuracy change during training.
rows.note: The text describes steadier improvement and stable performance through training completion; this gap does not establish the claimed curve.
rows.check: Stability gap for a reduced model. This does not measure an epoch-wise error curve shape.
